Tomato Paste Transfer Pump
Why Tomato Paste Requires a Special Pump
Tomato paste contains high solids and thick consistency. Standard pumps struggle with this viscosity.

A tomato paste transfer pump handles these conditions because rotary gears push product through the chamber at a constant rate. The pump does not rely on high speed. Instead, it uses controlled displacement.
This design helps you:
Maintain steady product flow
Prevent clogging
Reduce product waste
Protect paste texture and quality
Food plants often combine liquid transfer pumps with gear pump systems to manage different stages of processing.
How Rotary Gear Pumps Transfer Tomato Paste
Rotary gear pumps use two interlocking, rotating gears. These gears form a group of product in between the gear teeth and push it out toward the discharge area.
The system delivers constant flow even with thick products.
Key advantages
Handles high viscosity products
Maintains steady pressure
Requires low maintenance
Works well with food-grade materials
This makes the tomato paste transfer pump a preferred option for food factories.
Food engineers often recommend gear pumps for paste and sauce transfer.
Dr. Rajiv Sharma, a food processing engineer, explains:
“Positive displacement pumps such as gear pumps remain the most reliable equipment for transferring high viscosity foods like tomato paste.”
Many processing plants install liquid transfer pumps alongside gear pumps to handle different liquid products during processing.
